links.comparator_used: Original MedCalc-Bench labels (partly LLM-derived), used without the physician-in-the-loop audit and relabeling
links.outcome: Agreement with physician ground truth, and downstream accuracy of a model trained with RL on the labels, on physician-labeled instances
links.effect: Recomputed labels agreed with physician ground truth 74% of the time (95% CI 60-84%) versus 20% for the originals (95% CI 11-33%) on a 50-instance subset. The model trained on recomputed labels outperformed the one trained on originals by 13.5 percentage points (95% CI 10.6-16.6%). At least 27% of test labels were likely erroneous or incomputable. Evaluating frontier LLMs with the original labels underestimated their accuracy by 16-23 percentage points.
links.quote: In a controlled reinforcement-learning experiment, a model trained on recomputed labels outperforms one trained on originals by 13.5 percentage points (95% CI, 10.6-16.6%) on physician-labeled instances, and this advantage extends to related medical tasks.

design_hint: physician-in-the-loop label auditing of LLM-assisted benchmark
